summary: body.s-sad (L53) assigns --state-accent:var(--mid) and --state-bg:var(--ghost). VIOLATION: --mid (L23: rgba(255,255,255,.32)) is a structural dimming/secondary-text token with 5 non-emotional uses (L269 .blocker-text, L283 .verb-cmd.persist, L293 .gonogo-sub, L297 .station-status, L322 .ac-eyebrow span). --ghost (L25: rgba(255,255,255,.035)) is a structural hover-background token with 4 non-emotional uses (L120, L154, L188, L276). Both tokens violate the SA one-meaning rule: a token designed as structural UI opacity is serving as an emotional state accent. E67 question ('audit whether --slate-dim could double as sad-state neutral') resolved: BLOCKED. --slate-dim (proposed: rgba(148,163,184,.28)) has opacity .28 — insufficient for state-badge roles: L90 (border:1px solid var(--state-accent); color:var(--state-accent)) and L241 (.presence-mark: background:var(--state-accent); box-shadow:0 0 8px var(--state-accent)). A .28-opacity grey renders as near-invisible border text and a ghost glow dot — functionally unreadable as a state-badge accent. Proposed fix: new full-opacity token --stone:#a1adb8 (cool stone grey; warm-neutral, distinct from --slate:#94a3b8/scared by warmer undertone). New token family: --stone:#a1adb8; --stone-dim:rgba(161,173,184,.28); --stone-bg:rgba(161,173,184,.06). body.s-sad changes to --state-accent:var(--stone); --state-bg:var(--stone-bg).
